title: United Airlines Employee Threatens to Call ICE on Mexican-American Citizen at San Francisco Airport
excerpt: Julio Varela, a naturalized US citizen and California business owner, recorded the exchange over a ticketing error that has since gone viral, prompting United to investigate.
body:
• A United Airlines employee at San Francisco International Airport threatened to call ICE on a Mexican-American passenger during a dispute over a ticketing error, telling him "you don't act like a citizen."
  • Julio Varela, a naturalized US citizen and California business owner, recorded the exchange, which has since gone viral on Reddit and drawn widespread condemnation.
  • United Airlines says it is investigating the incident, and the employee's union confirmed she has been "held out of service pending further investigation."
  • The incident comes amid heightened immigration enforcement across the US, with ICE operations expanding into airports and public spaces.

A United Airlines employee at San Francisco International Airport threatened to call Immigration and Customs Enforcement on a Mexican-American passenger during a heated dispute over a ticketing error, telling him "you don't act like a citizen" in an exchange captured on video and now circulating widely on social media.

Julio Varela, a naturalized US citizen and business owner from San Ramon, California, was travelling to Montreal with his wife and two daughters when the confrontation took place earlier this month, according to reports from USA Today, NBC News, and Bay Area outlet KQED.

Hours of Frustration Over a Name Error

The dispute began with a simple booking mistake. Varela's wife had accidentally swapped their daughter's middle and last names when purchasing tickets online. The family spent roughly 15 hours over two weeks on the phone trying to resolve the issue before arriving at SFO, where they spent another three hours working with United and Air Canada staff, since the flight was booked through United but operated by Air Canada.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=hHvD44nwFr8

Air Canada managed to fix its side of the ticketing issue, but the United employee refused to update the remaining ticket, according to Varela. "She said, 'I'm not dealing with it, it ain't my problem,'" Varela told KQED.

When Varela pressed the employee for her name so he could file a complaint, the two began filming each other. The employee walked away into a restricted area before returning to the ticketing counter.

"Photo: Wikimedia Commons" style="max-width:100%;border-radius:8px" loading="lazy"><figcaption style="font-size:0.85rem;color:#666;margin-top:8px">San Francisco International Airport."

'Maybe We Should Call ICE on You'

In the follow-up video posted to Reddit, the employee tells Varela: "Maybe we should call ICE on you. 'Cause you don't act like a citizen. Get away."

https://x.com/TheOfficerTatum/status/2079323810893803802

"I am Mexican. I was born in Mexico, I am a U.S. citizen. I own my own business. I pay taxes. I employ people. For her, especially with what's going on right now in America, to say that to a minority, especially a Hispanic person, I think it's really, really hateful and it's really racist."

— Julio Varela, passenger

Varela told KQED that his 14-year-old daughter was crying during the confrontation. The family ultimately made their flight after another United employee stepped in and resolved the ticketing issue.

United and Union Respond

United Airlines said in a statement that it is "looking into the interaction in this video" but declined to share additional details. The International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers (IAM), the union representing the employee, confirmed to USA Today that the worker "is being held out of service pending further investigation."

https://www.instagram.com/p/DU6hq_9kzFp/

In a separate statement to NBC News, the union said the comments "do not reflect the views or values of the IAM Union" and that any resulting matters would be handled through established collective bargaining processes.

A Charged Climate

The incident unfolds against a backdrop of expanded immigration enforcement across the United States. ICE operations have grown more visible at airports, workplaces, and public spaces since the beginning of the year. The weaponization of immigration enforcement language against citizens and legal residents — particularly those who are Hispanic or of colour — has drawn concern from civil rights organizations.

For the Indian diaspora, the episode resonates with broader anxieties about racial profiling and the assumption that citizenship can be judged by appearance or accent. Indian Americans, many of whom are naturalized citizens, have reported similar experiences of being questioned about their status despite holding valid documentation.

What Happens Next

United has not disclosed what disciplinary action, if any, it will take against the employee. SFO did not respond to media requests for comment. The viral video has drawn hundreds of comments and widespread condemnation, adding to a string of high-profile airline customer service incidents that have sparked public outrage in recent years.
